title: Distinct neural processes link speech planning and execution

data_scope.modality: human intracranial EEG (iEEG), broadband high-gamma feature
data_scope.participants: not stated in the openly accessible text (Methods paywalled); neurosurgical patients at Duke University / Duke Comprehensive Epilepsy Center

electrodes_inferred.right_hemisphere: ~791 (from ANOVA df F(9,781) across 10 ROIs and F(2,788) across 3 networks)
electrodes_inferred.note: derived from reported degrees of freedom, not quoted verbatim

data_scope.task: pseudo-word repetition; CVC vs VCV syllable-structure contrast
data_scope.raw_data_access: restricted; de-identified raw iEEG available to academic researchers under a data use agreement

core_conclusion: Speech planning and execution are carried by two computationally distinct neural regimes. During planning, different levels of speech units are coded discretely at distinct prefrontal sites; these planned units are then dynamically integrated across cortical levels to guide execution. During execution, speech-motor regions generate continuous sequences that encode both the discrete sound units and their transitional (co-articulatory) properties. This rapid discrete-to-continuous handoff is the hinge linking planning to execution.
why_it_matters: Supplies a concrete mechanism for how planning hands control to articulation, makes the syllable-before-phoneme hierarchy temporally explicit (lead contracts from 250-350 ms in planning to 17-25 ms in monitoring), argues for stage- and region-aware speech neuroprosthesis decoders, and demonstrates that conclusions about neural coding depend on the spatial support of the recording electrode.
why_nature: Mechanism for a universal human behaviour; rare multi-scale human intracranial evidence irreplaceable by fMRI or scalp EEG; bridges psycholinguistics, systems neuroscience and neural-interface engineering; translational stakes for speech BCIs without over-claiming; strong reproducibility posture (Zenodo derived data, GitHub code, per-figure source data, disclosed LLM-assisted code verification).
added_value_to_my_research: Scale-swept graph operator over irregular sensor geometry -> a principled MAUP/spatial-support test for urban sensor networks
Switching state-space discrete-plan/continuous-execution model -> transition-aware modelling of mobility activity chains and telehealth substitution
Spatiotemporal attribution over contact x time x band -> validating XAI methods where anatomical ground truth exists, then porting to location x time x covariate stacks
Coordinate-conditioned embeddings + masked reconstruction -> multi-city geospatial foundation model that fine-tunes without forcing a common grid

Hierarchy-collapse law (coarse leads fine, lead contracts toward output) -> falsifiable lag hypothesis for urban hierarchies; plus 2SFCA/R2SFCA catchment analysis of who can reach speech-neuroprosthesis centres
